Quarterback situations

TeamSituation
WAKEGio Lopez was held out of the Merrimack game as a precaution and was reported available to start at SMU, so he is modeled as the starter over Steele Pizzella.
WISTrue freshman Ryan Hopkins started the last game with Colton Joseph hurt. Joseph is listed as emergency-only. Hopkins has thrown little, so Wisconsin passing numbers are low confidence.
MSSTAJ Swann has started since Kamario Taylor's season-ending surgery. He left the Texas game early. Mississippi State passing numbers are low confidence.
NUBackup Nicco Marchiol started the Iowa game. No starter is announced for Ohio State yet, so Northwestern passing numbers are low confidence.
OSULuke Fahey is modeled with Julian Sayin still out. Ohio State has not named a starter for this game, so passing numbers are low confidence.
KSUKansas State's quarterback is unconfirmed for TCU. Blake Barnett, modeled here, holds a small share of the season's attempts, so passing numbers are low confidence.
ASUJake Fette has started since Mikey Keene's knee injury, and Kenny Dillingham said he stays the starter. He is a freshman with a small sample.
TTUThomas Castellanos made his first Texas Tech start Nov 1 after his eligibility case. His Texas Tech sample is small.
BOISMax Cutforth replaced the injured Maddux Madsen against Texas State. Madsen's status for this game is unknown.
PITTESPN reported Mason Heintschel tore his ACL and is out for the season. Holden Geriner is Pitt's full-time starter, so the modeled starter is confirmed with high confidence.
UCLANico Iamaleava is expected to miss the rest of the season after knee surgery (Daily Bruin, Oct 12). Ty Dieffenbach has taken over, so the modeled starter is confirmed with high confidence.
UCFAlonza Barnett III is back from a hamstring injury and led the winning drive at Kansas. Keyone Jenkins is the questionable backup. Barnett as starter is likely, with medium-high confidence.
CLEMTait Reynolds has started since Christopher Vizzina's elbow injury in September, and Vizzina is listed out. No report names a different starter for Georgia Tech, so medium-high confidence.
KUThe AP preview lists Isaiah Marshall as the Kansas passing leader, and he won the job in camp. The questionable QB on the injury list is a backup, so high confidence.
MSUAlessio Milivojevic is the named starter and Cam Fancher, listed questionable, is the backup. Milivojevic missed the UCLA game in late October. No report this week says he is out, so his start is unconfirmed but likely.
MDMalik Washington is Maryland's returning starter. The questionable QB on the injury list is a backup. No report this week changes that, so he is unconfirmed but likely.
SYRA Nov 5 Field Level Media story covers Steve Angeli as Syracuse's quarterback. The questionable QB on the injury list is a backup, so high confidence.
NDCJ Carr is Notre Dame's starter. The QB listed out is a backup, so the injury does not affect the model.
USCJayden Maiava is USC's starter. The QB listed questionable is a backup, so the injury does not affect the model.
SCLaNorris Sellers is South Carolina's starter. The QB listed questionable is a backup, so the injury does not affect the model.

Starters on other teams come from the latest game played, skipping anyone listed out, not a confirmed announcement.

Player probabilities are close to honest. Holdout buckets landed within about 3 points of actual hit rates, except the top two, which ran 4 points high. Those high numbers now take a haircut, fit on the same holdout, so that correction has not been tested on new games.

Game lines show no edge. Spread MAE was 11.84 points for the close vs 13.06 for our line. Total MAE was 12.73 vs 13.26, across 291 games. The best-fit weight on our line was negative, so every game side here is a pass.

Prop value is unknown. No college prop lines were available, so no prop EV is claimed. The small sample covers six weeks of one season.

2026 holdout, all markets. Dots near the dashed line mean a forecast of X% hit about X% of the time.

Data gaps

  • Prop lines and prices: none found. Each game gives fair lines and limits instead. Moneyline, spread and total prices are real DraftKings numbers via ESPN.
  • Scheme: no man/zone, coverage shell, blitz or pressure rate, routes, alignment or snap counts exist in free college data. Throw location appears only in games with charted text. Nothing here is inferred from a coach's reputation.
  • Positions: roles come from usage, so tight ends show as WR.
  • Injuries: college has no required injury report. Covers is unofficial, and P(plays) values are assumptions. In the backtest 35% of eligible players did not log a stat, so absences are a large risk.
  • Sample: 2026 only for market-tied testing, because ESPN holds few 2025 lines.

Sources: ESPN, NWS, Covers injuries.

These are estimates, and no selection is guaranteed. After the games, run review_cfb.py to score every forecast (Phase 15).

Building a parlay Predictive

Conservative: Kwazi Gilmer 20+ receiving yds (85%) + Anthony Colandrea 150+ passing yds (84%). Joint estimate 74.4%, fair -290. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 76.7% vs 73.7% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Antwan Raymond 20+ rushing yds (80%) + Kwazi Gilmer 30+ receiving yds (79%) + Anthony Colandrea 175+ passing yds (78%). Joint estimate 53.4%, fair -115. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 57.2% vs 52.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Aggressive: Antwan Raymond 40+ rushing yds (62%) + Anthony Colandrea 30+ rushing yds (62%) + AJ Surace 150+ passing yds (62%). Joint estimate 23.4%, fair +327. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 25.7% vs 25.8% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Conservative: Braden Atkinson 150+ passing yds (94%) + Dylan Riley 20+ rushing yds (93%). Joint estimate 86.8%, fair -656. These legs are approximately independent: sim joint 96.0% vs 95.9% if independent. Not guaranteed.

Balanced: Braden Atkinson 225+ passing yds (79%) + Dylan Riley 50+ rushing yds (79%) + Jesse Legree 50+ receiving yds (78%). Joint estimate 52.8%, fair -112. These legs are positively correlated: sim joint 55.4% vs 51.1% if independent. Not guaranteed.
